In particular because the not-so-veiled insults are also insults against his mother. On a more humorous note, he's particula

characters.name: Novelverse
characters.description: All the Other Reindeer: After he becomes more openly emotional inEx Machina, other Vulcans start treating him like he's some sort of disgusting freak. One officer even requests a transfer rather than be on the sameshipas him. Spock, meanwhile, points out how veryemotionalthey're being. Character Development:"Forgotten History" shows him in the transitory state between the original series and where he is duringThe Motion Picture, deciding it's maybe time to really get around to finishing the Kohlinar."Ex Machina" is all about Spock coming to terms with the events ofThe Motion Picture, and becoming who we see inWrath of Khan, reconciling logic and emotion (and hopefully, without going off his nut like Sybok). "Forgotten History" shows him in the transitory state between the original series and where he is duringThe Motion Picture, deciding it's maybe time to really get around to finishing the Kohlinar. "Ex Machina" is all about Spock coming to terms with the events ofThe Motion Picture, and becoming who we see inWrath of Khan, reconciling logic and emotion (and hopefully, without going off his nut like Sybok). Coitus Ensues: To solve the issue of him and an alternate T'Pring being connected to one another, which lasts for several days. Her commander, a Vulcan, recognizes what's going on and covers for them.

characters.name: Kelvin Timeline
characters.description: A child born of aVulcan father and human mother, he facedHalf-Breed Discriminationmost of his life and chose to join Starfleet over the Vulcan Science Academy as he never felt welcomed by Vulcans. He would become a brilliant commander and science officer in Starfleet, acting as Pike's second-in-command and stepping in command when necessary. Eventually a James T. Kirk took command and Spock found his calling as hisNumber Two, offering purely logical advice while forming a deep friendship. Adaptational Personality Change: This Spock's emotions tend to be a bit closer to the surface than the original. Adorably Precocious Child:Justified. He was raised since birth to control his emotions, so he was surprisingly mature as a child. All of the Other Reindeer: Heavily implied given how he was verbally harassed by his classmates as a child and the Vulcan Council made insensitive comments about his human heritage. Badass Adorable/Pint-Sized Powerhouse: Lil' Spock. Beats up a teenager twice his size for calling his mother a "human whore".

characters.name: M'Ress
characters.description: M'Ress is from Cait, a planet of feline bipeds who have joined the Federation. She serves as the ship's relief communications officer when Lt. Uhura is off duty. Like Uhura, she sometimes acts as a temporary science officer when Mr. Spock is unavailable. Adaptation Species Change: In the comic book accompanying theAudio PlayPassage to Moauv, she's portrayed as ablue-skinned, green-haired humanoid. Adventurer Archaeologist: According toher official biography, archaeology is one of her interests, although the cartoon never shows this. Barefoot Cartoon Animal: She goes barefoot throughout the series. The official explanation is that she doesn't need (or want) footwear because of her thick pawpads, although the animators don't bother drawing them when her soles are visible. Cat Folk: She resembles a bipedal lioness, complete withPointy Ears, slit-shaped vertical pupils with yellow sclerae, a mane, a tail, and digitigrade legs. She also speaks with "a cat-like purring quality to her voice".

characters.name: Arex
characters.description: Lieutenant Arex is a male Edosian Starfleet officer who lives during the mid-23rd century. He serves as navigator on the U.S.S Enterprise in place of Pavel Chekov. Bizarre Alien Biology: He has three arms andtelepathy. Celibate Hero: While under Harry Mudd's love potion, he only plays a lute. Probably because he has no one of his species onboard the ship. Flat Character: He's mostly just a guy who responds to orders and does his job. Hidden Depths: He's quite good with his lute.

characters.name: Captain Jean-Luc Picard
characters.description: A seasoned starship captain and considered among the best Starfleet has to offer. Born and raised in La Barre, France (though possesses an English Yorkshire accent), he grew up on a vineyard with aluddite familyand afather who disapproved of his aspirationsfor exploration and adventure. He excelled at xenoarchaeologist and was fond of classical music and literature, particularlyShakespeare. Despite a reserved, stoic disposition in the present day he was known to bemore rebellious and competitiveat Starfleet Academy and in his early career, which after an encounter with some Nausicaans in aBar Brawlleft him withan artificial heart. Polymath, diplomat, andall-around gentleman, Picard rose through the ranks and as First Officer of the Stargazer his Commanding Officer was killed in battle andhe was forced to take charge. The victory of the battle resulted in himpromoted to Captainof the Stargazer afterwards. Among his close friends was Jack Crusher, who he sadly lost in an accident but maintains a complicated relationship with Jack's widow Beverly and son Wesley. The Stargazer was later lost in another conflict, later discovered to be an unknown early encounter with the Ferengi. This stalled his career for some time but did gain infamy for what became known as the Picard Maneuver in that battle, a warp-assistedFlash Step. Jean-Luc was sadly assimilated by the Borg and his knowledge unwillingly assisted them in the devastating Battle of Wolf 359, where 39 ships were lost totaling about 10,000 casualties. This would continue to haunt him, and despite multiple future encounters with the Borg would never shake what happened to him and what he did. He maintained close personal relationships with the other senior officers of theEnterprise-D, particularly Data, whose quest for humanity Picard took a special interest in. He would prove especially adept in aCourtroom Debates, arguing in favor of Data's sentience while also stemming off toxic witch hunts that were brewing in Star

characters.name: Commander William Riker
characters.description: The first officer of the Enterprise-D. While an immensely disciplined Starfleet Officer he is also known to beThe Charmerand heads turn his way whenever he shows up. He is fiercely loyal, he is probably the one officer whom Picard is most open with and is one to oppose the captain taking a hands-on approach to away missions. Riker is very charming and affable with his peers, though a fewLower Deck Episodesshow that his subordinates are intimidated by him as he demands a performance up to the standards of the fleet's flagship. His posting on the Enterprise came with an unusual situation where he had to work with Deanna Troi, a former love whomhe had left due to his career advancements. On an off again, they would eventually rekindle their romance. He also was forced to confront a transporter clone, anAlternate Selfwho was stranded on aDeath Worldfor 8 years while he enjoyed a successful career. The clone came to call himself Thomas Riker, using their middle name, before embarking on a different path. Although an excellent officer, Riker was notorious for refusing promotions so that he could stay on board theEnterprise, believing the first officer of the flagship to be more prestigious than captain of another ship while also hoping to inherit the Enterprise from Picard. Several alternate timelines or illusionary realities put him in the Captain's chair. After 15 years with Picard he finally accepts promotion to captain of the USS Titan with Deanna next to him. For tropes related to his appearances onStar Trek: Lower Decks, see the character sheetStar Trek: Lower Decks - Starfleet Ships. The Ace: Riker is good at everything. He's an inspiring leader, anAce Pilot, a badass fighter, a nice guy, a ladies' man, a skilled poker player, and a talented trombonist. Picard says that Riker's the best officer he'severworked with. Ace Pilot: Riker is famed among Starfleet for his piloting prowess. He establishes his credentials in "Encounter at Farpoint" with a manual spaceport do

characters.name: Lieutenant Commander Geordi La Forge
characters.description: Geordi was born blind and was given a specialized VISOR which works with implants in his head to give him sight, in fact he can see in EM ranges even tricorders may struggle with, but also causes chronic pain. Later on he received more straightforward ocular implants. He starts out as one of the ship's helmsmen sitting next to Data, but was promoted to Chief Engineer, making it his job to tell the captain that [insert engineering feat here] was impossible andthen do it within an absurdly short timeframe.While exceptional as an Engineer he had command aspirations, and in addition to several alternate timelines would be officially promoted to Commodore. One of Geordi's more prominent aspects was his friendship with Data. He often described himself as Data's best friend and was an eager assistant in the android's attempts to become more human. He spent some timeunlucky in lovebut would build some close friendships, and eventually gather a family with multiple daughters. All Love Is Unrequited: He can never seem to get the girl. Creator interviews suggest that this is partly because Geordi is in love with theEnterprise, similar to the way that Kirk was (although it is much less of aMasochism Tango). His relationship with the holographic Leah Brahms, the ship's designer, evokes this. Aura Vision: Occasionally the crew (and audience) gets to see what Geordi sees, which appears as a confusing mass of light and color. Geordi explains that he can choose what to focus on the same way he can focus on one conversation in a crowded room. In the bookMetamorphosis, Geordi describes organic beings as having a shifting aura around them. Data's more machine nature has his aura look like ahalo. When Databecomes human, Geordi observes that he's "lost his halo". Beware the Nice Ones: One of the nicest characters on the show, but in "The Next Phase" he stillshoved an armed Romulan agent into the vacuum of spaceto save Ro.

characters.name: Lieutenant Natasha "Tasha" Yar
characters.description: TheEnterprise-D'sChief of Security, she grew up on a failed human colony that devolved into gang warfare, drug smuggling and environmental disasters. Starfleet was a chance to escape that life, though she left behind her sister Ishara. Tragically, she was suddenly killed by a creature named Armus as a display of its power. While under the influence of a virus she expressed romantic interest in Data, and after her death he spoke fondly of her and the chance to explore his own relationships. She does reappear in other events surrounding alternate timelines, oneAlternate Selflived while the Federation was at war with the Klingons, but learning of the original timeline where she died a meaningless death she chose to helpSet Right What Once Went Wrongeven if it resulted in aHeroic Sacrifice. This chain of events resulted in her conceiving a half-Romulan daughter named Sela. Ambiguously Bi: In “The Naked Now”, she talks like she’s always had a crush on Deanna, and touches her hand for long enough that Deanna looks questioning. Attack! Attack! Attack!: She suggests the (impractical and provocative) plan of blasting their way free of any situation. Back for the Dead: The episode "Yesterday's Enterprise." Tasha's meaningless death in the original timeline was discussed by her and Guinan, and Tasha decided that, if she was going to be "killed" by the restoration of the timeline, she would rather make aHeroic Sacrificewith the crew of theEnterprise-C.

characters.name: Lieutenant (later Lieutenant Commander) Worf
characters.description: A Klingon adopted by humans after his parents were killed in a Romulan attack on Khitomer, Worf was the first Klingon Starfleet Officer and joined due to the influence of his Starfleet parents. In most respects he aspires to the ideals of theProud Warrior Racebetter than most native-born Klingons, and finds himself having to defend his family house against the political machinations of groups within the Klingon High Command. He had a romantic partner in K'Ehleyr, which produced a son named Alexander, who for a time was sent to Worf's adopted parents. He is a committed Starfleet Officer but his natural Klingon culture is often challenged by the more pacifistic nature of the Federation and Starfleet. Beginning as a Lieutenant Junior Grade, he was primarily a multi-function bridge officer before the death of Tasha Yar saw him promoted to Lieutenant, Chief of Security and a Senior Officer. He was the primary reference source when dealing with Klingon matters and ever vigilant in possible dangers to the Enterprise and its crew. He also had a brief romance with Deanna Troi, which he later attributes to him growing into a more confidentWarrior Poet. See theWorfcharacter page for further details.

characters.name: Doctor (Commander) Beverly Crusher
characters.description: Chief Medical Officer of the Enterprise, she brings with her a teenage son Wesley. Has a long and complicated relationship with Picard, who served over her late husband, Jack Crusher, as Captain of the ill-fatedStargazer. Picard, still troubled with guilt over Jack's death, causes a lot of uncomfortable feelings between them. She transferred to Starfleet Medical for a year, leaving Wesley behind as an Acting Ensign under Picard's supervision, she returned to the Enterprise with a desire to not miss any more of Wesley's childhood. Compassionate to a fault, she will sometimes take big risks for the sake of helping her patients or rooting out conspiracies even at the risk of her career. Despite her general disposition being warm and maternal,she is surprisingly quick with a phaserand has sometimes dropkicked the bad guys. She also has a background of music and dance, which she has tried to minimize in her career due to anEmbarrassing Nicknameof "The Dancing Doctor." Action Mom: She's pretty good whenever she has to use combat skills and not medical ones. She also has the best aiming skills of the entire main cast. In "Descent Part II," she's left in charge of Enterprise with a fraction of the normal crew, all no-names, while all the main cast is off hunting for Data. She takes on the Borg andwins. The Bus Came Back: After spending Season 2 away at Starfleet Medical, Crusher returns to theEnterprisein Season 3 and remains there for the rest of the series and the movies. The Cast Show Off: GatesMcFaddenmade her name as a choreographer and, in "Data's Day," Crusher gets a scene where she teaches Data to dance, opening with a fairly impressive bit of tap-dancing from the doctor. Crusher, ironically, isn't too keen on word of her talents getting around the ship, not wanting to be known as "the dancing doctor"again.

characters.name: Counselor (Lieutenant Commander, later Commander) Deanna Troi
characters.description: Half-Betazoid counselor who Picard requested to sit right next to him onThe Bridge. This is justified by her empathic abilities, which allowed her to detect lies and therefore give an edge to Picard in negotiations (though mostlystated the obvious). Her posting on the Enterprise caused some difficulty with Will Riker, as they had a past romantic history which would be explored and later renewed. Despite a high rank of Lieutenant Commander, in lieu of the standard Starfleet uniform wore a multitude offeminized outfitsin an attempt to not intimidate subordinates. When Captain Jellico took temporary command of theEnterprise, he promptly told her to change into a proper uniform. After a culmination of multiple events, including changing outfits and dealing with a crisis, she sought further training and would pass the bridge officer's test and become a commander. Troi is also notable for her very,verymeddlesome mother (Lwaxana). She also had a brief romantic relationship with Worf, which lead to a deep respect for each other even if it didn't work out. '80s Hair: Troi looks like a hard rock singer with her massive frizzy hair and miniskirt in "Farpoint". They didn't start to get her hair under control untilFirst Contact. An Alien Named "Bob": Downplayed. Deanna isonly half alien. Boomerang Bigot: Despite being half-human, Deanna will sometimes voice her low opinion of humans. Deanna (unlike Spock) doesn't really face an identity crisis as a result of her two races not getting along (Betazoids and humans are friendly Federation allies). She simply likes the cool powers that her non-human side gives her, so her need to feel superiority in her alien heritage comes across as arrogant. It's not until "The Loss" that someone (Riker, no less)calls her out on it. And it seems to have worked.

characters.name: Lieutenant Commander Data
characters.description: A gold-skinned android who serves as Operations Officer aboard theEnterprise, and the Second Officer of the ship after Commander Riker. He was created by an eccentric scientist named Noonien Soong looking to create an independent positronic brain. Soong also created a large number of other androids, some more advanced than others, but most notably his near identical "brother" named Lore. Abandoned on a planet with his memory wiped, his retrieval by Starfleet is the first thing he remembers and reasoned that his natural path was to enroll in Starfleet Academy. Data's fascination with the human existence drives many of his actions. Officially he lacks emotions, but does understand friendship, loyalty and even explores romantic relationships including with Tasha Yar. Forever NOT human, he possesses incredible calculation abilities, physical strength while also having an inability to use contractions. He grows especially close to Geordi, while Picard champions his right as an individual as others in Starfleet see him asJust a Machine. His speed, calculation and vocal mimicry has proven to be potentially devastating when he is logged into a starship computer, which makes everyone grateful he is on their side.

characters.name: Ensign Wesley Crusher
characters.description: The teenage son of Dr. Beverly Crusher, he is aTeen Geniuswith aspirations to join Starfleet but constantly finding problems scheduling tests and getting to transports to the Academy with all the adventures of the Enterprise. To commend him for his services to the ship Picard grants him the rank of Acting Ensign, if only to allow him the minimum of bridge access, and later aField Promotionto full Ensignbeforehe left to attend Starfleet Academy. He does struggle with the expectations placed on him, and an incident at the Academy makes him realize that doing the right thing sometimes forces him to admit his mistakes. Early on he encountered an alien called The Traveler who has access to abilities outside of time and space, and whom said that Wesley has a great destiny in front of him. Always Second Best: He was beaten into the Academy by his Benzite colleague Mordock, though the episode never actually shows why Mordock was judged superior. Author Avatar:Eugene Wesley Roddenberryopenly admitted that Wesley Crusher was ayounger, idealized version of himself. Oddly enough, though, the character was originally envisioned asa teenaged girl named Leslie.Even in real life. When Wesley aced his second entrance exam for the Academy, Roddenberry commemorated it by presenting Wil with the second lieutenant bars Gene earned in the Air Corps. Present at the ceremony was General Colin Powell! Eugene Wesley Roddenberryopenly admitted that Wesley Crusher was ayounger, idealized version of himself. When Wesley aced his second entrance exam for the Academy, Roddenberry commemorated it by presenting Wil with the second lieutenant bars Gene earned in the Air Corps. characters.name: TheEnterprise-D
characters.description: The fifth Federation ship to bear the nameEnterprise. Among the firstGalaxy-class starships, theEnterprise-D is just as much of a character as her crew. Designed for long-range deep space exploration to the pointthat she carries a significant civilian population, including family units, on board. Like other Enterprise's, it is treated as the flagship of Starfleet, staffed with the best crew available. The Artifact: TheGalaxy-class was designed the way it was because it was thought that its saucer separation abilities would arise frequently, but it took too long, and it was used only three times on the show: the pilot episode "Encounter at Farpoint", "The Arsenal of Freedom" (also from season 1), and "The Best of Both Worlds: Part II" from season 4, before being used for the last time inStar Trek: Generations.For a ship designated as the "flagship" of the Federation, she rarely acted in that manner as we would understand it in relation to Earth navies. She doesn't have an admiral and staff on board and rarely leads any squadrons of Federation ships. Instead she was treated more like a patrol & long range exploration vessel. The only time theEnterpriseserved as the command ship of a fleet was during the Klingon Civil War, and even then, the Fleet Admiral who approved Picard's plan of blockading the Romulan border to keep them from interfering gave Picard broad discretion to command the fleet as he saw fit (which included transferring Riker, Data, and Geordi to other understaffed ships), rather than travel with the fleet.There was also an alternate universe where theEnterprisewas leading a war against the Klingons, in which the ship was much more military than the original one. characters.name: Lieutenant Reginald Barclay
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolanderand social basketcase who serves aboard theEnterpriseas engineer. Has logged more holodeck hours than even Riker himself; in fact, Barclay practicallyliveson the holodeck, which renders him useful whenever some quirkyHolodeck Malfunctionhappens. Barclay later turned up onVoyager, where his holodeck OCD somehow led to a communications breakthrough, allowing Starfleet to detect Janeway's stranded crew. It can be safely said that Barclay is more at ease around computers than people. Unsurprisingly, his closest friend ended up being Dr. Zimmerman, taciturn and antisocial creator of the EMH. Almighty Janitor: He's a low-level member of the general engineering staff, but he's good when the spotlight's on him. This is even more apparent in his appearances on Voyager. Years after leaving theEnterprise, he's still just a lowly lieutenant, but he's also the head of an entire division of Starfleet Communications and in charge of finding a way to bringVoyagerhome. He reports directly to a four pip admiral. Brain Critical Mass: In "The Nth Degree," Barclay's brain is taken over by an ancient race from the center of the galaxy, greatly increasing his intellect. Under their influence, Barclay seizes command of theEnterprise, controlling the ship with his mind. Brainwash Residue: The end of "The Nth Degree" implies he may have retained some of the increased knowledge he temporarily acquired since he now suddenly knows how to play chess when he didn't before.

characters.name: Guinan
characters.description: Wise and mysterious bartender with a big hat. Guinan manages the Ten Forward lounge, but her history with Picard goes back way further than that. Contrary to appearance, she is one of the last survivors of an ageless and inscrutable species who were scattered by the Borg. Most of her past remains murky; she harbors no love for Q, and is possibly the one person he truly fears. In the TNG films, Guinan is revealed to have once been trapped in the Nexus. Almighty Janitor: In "Yesterday's Enterprise," Picard sends 120 people to their deaths on the word of abartenderwho can tell that the timeline is out of sorts. Badass Bystander: Calming down abrewingbarfight in Ten-Forward by firing an impressive-looking phaser into the ceiling.noteOn Setting 1, for those wondering how this didn't cause major damageAnd there are hints that she has some sort of hidden power that could let her go one on one with Q of all people. Bartender Confidant: Her main role in the show is usually to give advice to the other crew. Sometimes overlaps withTrickster Mentorwhen she deliberately irritates people to get them to figure something out, as with Worf or Ro. Berserk Button: For as patient and calm as she is, dealing with the Borg truly upsets her, to the point where she refuses to even listen to any positive comments about them, despite coming from a race of "listeners." It'sjustifiedin that the Borg decimated the El-Aurians through assimilation, leaving Guinan and the few surviving others in her race scattered and alone throughout the galaxy.

characters.name: Keiko Ishikawa O'Brien
characters.description: A botanist who worked in theEnterprisearboretum. Later introduced to her eventual husband, Miles O'Brien, throughmatchmakerData. As the most stable family unit onStar Trek, the O'Briens nonetheless had their share of problems. A majority of "O'Brien Must Suffer" episodes revolve around Keiko and/or Molly being placed in imminent peril. When O'Brien left to joinDeep Space Nine, Keiko and their daughter Molly came with him. Keiko opened a children's school on the station. Born in an Elevator: Gave birth to her daughter Molly in the ship's lounge in the midst of a crisis.With Worf delivering the baby. Put on a Bus: ToDeep Space Ninealong with her husband Miles.

characters.name: Transporter Chief Miles O'Brien
characters.description: Perennially unlucky Irishman, put in charge of the transporter room. A veteran of numerous never-seen wars, most notably the Cardassian conflict, which lands him squarely on the ideological side of the Maquis. Unlike Ro Laren and Wesley, though, he stayed true to the uniform. O'Brien later transferred toDeep Space Nineas its chief engineer. Though his character growth was limited, he was featured much more prominently on a show in which evenan extragot his own episode at some point. He's also one of the few members of Starfleet ever depicted to be enlisted. A Day in the Limelight: The episode "The Wounded," about his and his old captain's experience in the Cardassian war. Ascended Extra: Colm Meaney looks soyoungin "Encounter at Farpoint". He went from an unnamed speaking bridge officer in the pilot to a recurring minor character to a main character onDeep Space Nine. Ironically, Meaney was never interested in pursuing a regular role because the loose TNG schedule afforded him time to do other things. Alas, he was much too talented to waste in the transporter room. (Shades of Robert Picardo.)In fact, he reallywasjust an extra in "Encounter at Farpoint": the character is not named and is just theRed Shirtmanning Navigation, wearing the rank of Ensign. He would later appear in his more familiar role in the Transporter room, as alieutenant, but referred to as the "transporter chief". He wouldn't get a full name or his more familiar rank of Chief Petty Officer until several seasons into the show. All that said, itisMiles O'Brien in each appearance and not just Colm Meaney playing several characters, as "All Good Things" retcons his first appearance in "Encounter at Farpoint" as specifically being O'Brien. characters.name: Molly O'Brien
characters.description: Miles and Keiko O'Brien's first child. Had the dubious honor of being delivered by Worf. Her baby brother, Kirayoshi O'Brien, is born under similarly weird circumstances. Daddy's Girl: She has a strong bond with her father. Put on a Bus: She's written out of most of season 3 and 4 when she and her mother leave for a botanical trip to Bajor. She's still relatively important as a motivator for Miles and she and her motherdo return, although with a diminished role. Soap Opera Rapid Aging Syndrome: She was born in TNG's fifth season, but in TNG's sixth season episode "Rascals," only a couple months beforeDS9's premiere, she was already a toddler who could speak. Less egregious than most examples since Hana Hatae played Molly from "Rascals" throughDS9's entire run. Wild Child: Her most plot-relevant role is in "Time's Orphan", when she ends up stranded alone on a planet for a decade and loses her faculty of language. This is undone at the end of the episodewhen she saves her past self.

characters.name: Nurse (Ensign, later Lieutenant) Alyssa Ogawa
characters.description: Dr. Crusher's assistant in sickbay, and a frequentMauve Shirt(though she survived each ordeal). Ascended Extra: Many of her initial appearances were as an unnamed medic helping Crusher. Combat Medic: Downplayed, as she has few if any outrightAction Girlmoments but is a sickbay nurse who keeps calm and handles herself well when caught in the middle of a violent crisis, such as when the Borg storm the ship during the First Contact time travel incident. Creator's Pet: Ron Wilkerson and Jean Louise Matthias used the character often, especially in "Lower Decks", because they really liked the character.invoked Fake Guest Star: She appeareda lotduring the series.

characters.name: Doctor (Commander) Katherine Pulaski
characters.description: When GatesMcFaddenquit the show in its second season, Pulaski was brought on to replace her. An expy of Dr.McCoy, Pulaski was meant as aJerk with a Heart of Gold, including having an adversarial relationship with Data, whom she's uncomfortable with for being a machine. Long story short, her intended dynamics weren't received as well asMcCoy's, ultimately leading to everyone wanting Crusher back. While Pulaski was dropped from TNG with little fanfare, and replaced with GatesMcFaddenagain, the tendency has been for fans tonever let her live downher worst moments, and act as if her earliest characterization is her only characterization. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome:WhenMcFaddenreturned for Season 3, Pulaski dropped off the face of the galaxy with her last episode being aClip Show. She is mentioned in two further TNG episodes and the finale ofVoyager(being paged at Starfleet Medical), and shows up in theStar Trek Expanded Universemore than once.What's surprising is that when the holographic Moriarty returns in Season 6, he doesn't ask where Pulaski has gone. She was the one he spent the most time with, after all, so you would think that ifanybodywould mention her, he would.
